segments.text: A man wakes up in the ocean. At night. No ship. No life jacket. And no idea how he got there.
No chance. Nobody falls off a cruise ship, wakes up in the dark, and lives to tell it. Let's go look.
November twenty-third, {2022|twenty twenty two}. Thanksgiving eve. The Carnival Valor leaves New Orleans, bound for Cozumel, Mexico.
On board is James Michael Grimes, {28|twenty eight}, from Lafayette, Alabama. He is travelling with {18|eighteen} members of his family.
That first day, he enters an air guitar contest. And wins it. The prize is a free drink. He says he'd had drinks, but he was not drunk.
Around eleven that night, he is at a bar with his sister. He leaves to find the restroom. He never comes back.
What happened next, nobody knows. Not even James. He doesn't remember the walk. He doesn't remember the fall.
He comes to in the Gulf of Mexico. In the water, with no boat in sight. He says his worst fear is drowning. And he says he can't float.
So he swims. And he treads water. Hour after hour. The water is about seventy degrees. That sounds warm, until you spend a night in it.
And the ship? The ship sails on toward Mexico. Nobody raises the alarm until the next day.
Out in the dark, he swims through two schools of jellyfish. Then the sun comes up. He is still alone.
Then he sees a fin. Something with a flat mouth bumps his leg. He doesn't think it was a shark. That would not comfort me.
A stick floats by. It looks like bamboo. He chews on it, just to taste something that isn't salt water.
Noon, Thanksgiving Day. His sister reports him missing. The ship calls for him over the speakers. Security searches the decks with his photo.
Around {2:30|two thirty}, the ship calls the Coast Guard. Then the Valor turns around and retraces its route.

The Coast Guard launches a helicopter from New Orleans, a boat from Venice, and a plane from Mobile. The search area is more than {7,000|seven thousand} square nautical miles. Roughly the size of Massachusetts.
One head, in that much water. And nobody knows when he went in. I've seen better odds on a lottery ticket.
Evening. James sees lights. A ship. He swims for it.
And he waves the only thing he has. His socks. The rescue swimmer later called it a Hail Mary. Nobody spots socks.
{8:25|Eight twenty five} P M. About {20|twenty} miles south of Southwest Pass, Louisiana. The crew of a bulk carrier called Crinis is watching the water. They see him.
A Coast Guard Jayhawk helicopter lowers a rescue swimmer, Richard Hoefle. James collapses into the sling. Hoefle's best guess: between a minute and thirty seconds left.
He is in shock, mildly hypothermic, and badly dehydrated. He says he spent four days in intensive care, and lost twenty pounds. But he is alive.
The officer who ran the search had seventeen years on the job. He said this case was unlike anything he had been part of.
And James? He says he would go on another cruise. He just might not get within ten foot of the rails.
Up to {20|twenty} hours in open water. No jacket. No boat. I was wrong. Case closed.
